spec.title: ZAP: agreed intent and sustained autonomous execution

status.comment: The methodology and runtime are implemented independently of any campaign. Publishing, installation, and import do not activate a campaign; the coordinator confirms final requirement status against the complete denominator and stored evidence, without an additional approval ceremony.

p.METHOD-STATUS: ZAP serves campaigns that, after initial agreement, may run for hours, days, or weeks across sessions and executors. Its goal is a valuable verified result in the sense of Owner intent. New knowledge causes reassessment of uncertainty, value, feasibility, the current expected outcome, and the route. The concrete outcome may change within the authorized tradeoff space; the initial task list is not an immutable goal. Duration is not limited to one task or conversation. This document defines the contract and does not itself authorize execution.

p.METHOD-FOUNDATION: ZAP extends lossless planning, central acceptance, focused verification, parallel-work coordination, and multi-user-planning recovery. Permanent foundations are listed in the sources section. It adds an Owner-controlled autonomy charter, a fact graph, and explicit lowering. Publishing or installing the package does not replace a campaign-specific charter.

p.METHOD-CAPABILITY-BOUNDARY: Implemented operations are defined by the actual capabilities registries and machine command contract. The CLI, control service, persistent coordinator, and backend do not enlarge authority: import remains draft, an observation is not acceptance, and unsupported operations are refused.

p.AUTHORING-LANGUAGE: ZAP-authored specifications, public documentation, skills, and examples are written in English. Preserved imported sources and legacy payloads remain byte-faithful, and intentional Unicode fixtures may retain the exact data under test. Protocol identifiers, hashes, addresses, and source captures are never translated.

p.OWNER-DRAFT: The first pass with the Owner defines the valuable final outcome, work boundaries, mandatory properties, priorities, acceptable tradeoffs, and how completion will be verified. The coordinator investigates available facts and asks only intent questions those facts cannot answer. Dependent questions follow their prerequisites; independent research may continue in parallel.

p.OWNER-CHOICE-PRESENTATION: An Owner question explains the practical consequence in plain language, offers distinct options, and gives a recommendation with a reason. An unknown fact is not replaced with a convenient answer choice. An accepted decision is reused until material grounds change; asking again must identify what changed.

p.CHARTER-CONTENTS: The autonomy charter binds the campaign and initial state to the Owner mandate. It distinguishes required benefit, essential constraints, and admissible approximations; defines delegated technical and priority decisions, reserved decisions, permitted external actions, and stop rules. Outcome hypotheses may change inside this space without renegotiating the charter after every discovery. Resource and recovery settings are recorded where needed; absence of a numeric limit is not replaced with an invented global cap.

p.CHARTER-AUTHORITY: The Owner controls accepted charter terms separately from the agent-editable plan. An agent may prepare a draft, explanation, or amendment proposal. Changing a task, note, local file, or author field does not create authority. Verifiable Owner-command provenance comes from a trusted control adapter outside agent-editable state.

p.CHARTER-ACTIVATION: A charter is drafted first; the Owner then explicitly activates the exact revision for the named campaign through the trusted control service. An opaque credential is bound outside the editable store to a role, campaign, and allowed actions. Import, installation, harness mode, and an owner field neither activate the charter nor start the campaign.

p.LEGACY-AUTHORITY: Charter preparation explicitly classifies every imported constraint as retained unchanged, requiring an Owner decision, or explicitly replaced by the Owner. Import preserves original wording and provenance. For the NEXT pilot this includes the prohibition on starting implementation, NEXT-EXECUTION-AUTHORITY, unresolved D-022, and applicable publication constraints. Unknown classification does not remove a constraint; successful import does not start NEXT.

p.CHARTER-AMENDMENT: New Owner terms create a new charter revision with rationale and scope; the previous revision remains available. Unstarted proposals are reassessed under the active revision. Started operations are reconciled with it before the next permitted boundary. An agent cannot rewrite an accepted rule or erase a prior trigger to continue work.

stopping.title: 3. Stop conditions and actual inability to continue

p.OWNER-STOP-LAW: A methodological pause arises from an Owner command or an accepted charter condition. The coordinator adds no mandatory question of its own after every decision, stage, commit, or model change. Existing environment, authority, and tool constraints remain: an impossible or unauthorized action does not become permitted merely to keep work continuous.

p.RULE-EVALUATION: A rule has a stable identity and revision. Its expression uses explicitly supported operations over typed values, such as logical composition, value comparison, and counts of confirmed outcomes. The evaluator validates the expression and its inputs deterministically. It neither claims arbitrary natural language is algorithmically understood nor executes rule text as code.

p.SEMANTIC-ASSESSMENT: A semantic condition, such as whether a format change affects user-data migration, receives a separate agent assessment. The record names the proposed action, rule revision, data scope, sources, material basis, and result. The machine may verify the record and evaluate an expression over its result; the semantic conclusion still requires evidence and available verification. The assessment does not acquire Owner authority.

p.UNKNOWN-CONDITION: Insufficient data for a condition yields needs_evidence. The coordinator investigates the missing fact and does not begin an action whose permission or stop condition is unknown. Unknown is not converted to false or presented as a confirmed trigger. If required evidence is unavailable, the wait and its reason are recorded; this does not invent a stop policy.

p.WHOLE-CAMPAIGN-STOP: The Owner-selected default for a triggered condition is a whole-campaign stop. No new task or approach starts. Running executors perform only what is necessary to reach the declared safe boundary and preserve artifacts. Collecting surviving evidence and preparing material for an Owner decision are allowed; continuing product work under the name of preparation is not. Resume follows an Owner command and the active charter revision.

p.STICKY-PAUSE: A pause persists until an accepted Owner command binds its exact pause ID and current hash. Scoped pauses coexist; a campaign pause dominates. Stop delivery and actual safe state are observed separately. A missing signal, node or session change, or agent explanation does not clear the pause.

p.RESUME-AND-RULES: Resume does not disable later stop conditions. The Owner may permit exactly one prepared action by binding an exception to the rule, pause ID, and command-content identity. Only the Owner may begin a new approach-counting epoch or source cursor; prior history remains. Without that decision an agent does not reset counters or rename the problem to avoid retriggering.

p.APPROACH-IDENTITY: An architectural approach is bound to one problem and its source assumptions: its hypothesis, material solution method, and result criterion are named. Repeating a command after overload, fixing a typo, and adding a check to the same solution are not new architectural approaches. Renaming a task, using a new worker, or starting a new session does not reset problem history. Semantic equivalence of attempts receives a reasoned assessment rather than being inferred from matching names.

p.OWNER-STOP-EXAMPLES: Example Owner rules stop before a public-format change that affects user-data migration and present options after two failed architectural approaches to one problem. Failures are counted per problem across the campaign; failures on different problems do not add together, and changing the current task does not hide earlier outcomes. The campaign reaches a safe boundary, no third approach starts, and reviewing evidence or preparing an option comparison remains allowed.

p.RULE-TIMING: A before-action condition is evaluated against the captured proposal before its effect begins. A check after execution may expose a violation but is recorded as too_late, not as prevention. Changing prepared command content requires reassessment, and a before-next-action threshold does not authorize one more action.

p.WAIT-VERSUS-PAUSE: An unavailable server, exhausted quota, occupied resource, unknown external outcome, or unavailable evidence is recorded as an actual wait or inability to perform a specific step. It is neither campaign completion nor an Owner-rule trigger. Independent authorized work may continue unless a campaign stop applies; the reason, observed state, and retry condition remain visible.

p.CORE-OBJECTS: ZAP's core objects are Owner intent and charter, expected-outcome revisions, value and feasibility assessments, obligations, work nodes, facts, evidence, decisions, unknown regions, approaches, events, and projections. An obligation states required benefit or a guarantee for an outcome revision; a task is the current way to obtain it. Replacing a method does not erase the obligation. An authorized outcome revision may change applicability only with an explicit disposition and provenance. The graph links grounds to dependent decisions, work, and checks.

p.ORTHOGONAL-AXES: work_type identifies purpose: evidence, decision, change, verification, or integration. delivery_route is direct or an ordered set of applicable stages. Declared maturity is unspecified, prototype, functional, or productized; achieved maturity separately requires stage evidence and scoped acceptance. These axes are independent of node.kind and execution state. node.classified is only a declared annotation and proves neither maturity nor consumer readiness. Imported names do not infer classification; absence stays explicit.

p.UNKNOWN-REGIONS: A broad unknown region within the mandate, a precise research question, and a deliberately excluded region are different records. A broad region need only be bounded by the desired result and next refinement trigger; the whole world need not be atomized in advance. Exclusion requires authority and a reason. Lack of knowledge is not exclusion.

p.KNOWLEDGE-STATE: Knowledge records distinguish an unexamined region, a bounded question, evidence-supported knowledge, invalidated knowledge, and a region currently irrelevant to the selected route. Relevance may change when facts or the outcome change. A source capture identifies content but does not itself prove truth, applicability, or complete dependency closure.

p.FACT-EVIDENCE-DISTINCTION: A normative fact states a requirement and its specification status. An observation reports measured state of a specific subject; acceptance establishes a specific obligation. A fact marker or impl/done status alone does not prove current code behavior. Sources carry content identity and conclusions show their premises. Uncalibrated model-confidence percentages do not replace evidence.

p.DECISION-RECORD: A material decision stores concise alternatives, the choice, rationale, sources, authority, consequences, and review trigger. It preserves conclusions and enough grounds for reassessment rather than hidden reasoning. Changed or disproved grounds mark affected conclusions for review while preserving the old record as history. Repeated questions are compared by stable obligation and captured premises.

p.PROMOTE-FACTS: An executor finding begins as a candidate. After verification, knowledge needed by other developers is promoted into a permanent specification, test, document, or other accepted project source with an addressable anchor. A local plan, event log, or worker report does not become the sole store of accepted project law. Source and evidence links remain with the promoted fact.

p.RECURSIVE-LOOP: The cycle is recursive: intent and expected outcome lead to unknown questions, facts, decisions, a work graph, valuable action, and a new observation. The same form applies to a campaign, workstream, or inner task. Active obligations, constraints, inputs, and acceptance flow downward; artifacts, evidence, and grounds for review flow upward. Canon: spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-ADAPTIVE-CYCLE#root. This revises direction within the mandate as well as refining an old list.

p.LOWERING-CONTRACT: Lowering turns a large outcome into executable tasks or internal stages. Input contains final acceptance, material invariants, available sources, dependencies, change scope, and delegated decisions. Output names concrete inputs, write and integration owners, expected behavior, selected checks, evidence, and safe boundary. A future command or test is marked as needing creation; detailed wording does not make it exist.

p.LOWERING-CONSERVATION: Lowering preserves obligations of the active outcome revision: every item receives implementation and verification, every deferral a closure location, and every new work item provenance. Outcome revision is separate: an old item may be retained, replaced, excluded under an authorized tradeoff, or found unattainable under named conditions; its history and unmet portion remain visible. Refining subwork does not cancel an obligation. Parent acceptance verifies integration and current parent criteria. Link and coverage checks are algorithmic; evidence meaning and sufficiency are assessed separately.

p.LOWERING-BOUNDARY: Recursion stops at a comprehensible action with a cheap sufficient check. Direct execution is allowed without extra planning. Distant work stays coarse with known obligations and a refinement trigger. Repeated lowering must resolve named uncertainty or a defect in the prior decomposition. Route corrections preserve earlier decisions and change reasons.

p.MATURITY-ROUTES: Each outcome uses a sufficient route: direct execution; prototype followed by a finished solution; functional MVP followed by productization; or all three stages. Stages may remain inside one task. The 212 tasks are not automatically expanded into 636 stages. The route is justified by uncertainty, complexity, and verification cost.

p.STAGE-EXITS: A prototype completes a testable experiment and produces a conclusion, including a valuable disproof. A functional result implements the entire stated task scenario with material negative and recovery cases while keeping limitations visible. A productized result closes the full final contract and mandatory deferrals. An experiment may be accepted as an experiment; a consumer receives only established guarantees. An MVP bug does not become a requirement because a test records it.

p.FORMAL-DEFERRALS: The charter and packet may preauthorize suitable temporary deferral categories, including card and traceability work, final file organization, some architectural shells, doctests, and similar formal work. Actual scope is refined from the stage result. A deferral names its scope, reason, current-stage guarantees, owner, and evidence-backed closure obligation. A prototype need not first undergo full productization to receive this permission.

p.DEFERRAL-EXPOSURE: Deferral depends on requirement meaning and actual result use. If a standard shell protects an essential invariant, the temporary implementation protects it another way. Authority, truthful results, and preservation of actually affected data apply immediately. Isolated format research need not provide every public-migration guarantee; use by real consumers requires guarantees matching that use.

p.PROVISIONAL-INTEGRATION: A prototype or MVP may remain in a separate worktree, branch, or marked experimental area with controlled connection. A commit records an artifact; it does not prove product readiness. Missing formal checks remain explicit, and widening a shared ratchet baseline or disabling a global gate does not close a deferral. Final acceptance discharges every required obligation; early use separately conforms to the charter and impact scope.

p.PRODUCTION-PATH-PROBE: When it is unknown whether the architecture can satisfy final constraints, one representative slice is brought to those constraints early. It tests a specific risk such as a type boundary, serialization, or recovery. This is not an extra mandatory stage for every task. Rewriting a prototype preserves verified observations, independent behavior examples, and reasons for abandoning approaches.

p.GLOBAL-PROTOTYPE-STATE: Productizing one capability does not declare all of VibeVM beyond its overall prototype state. Product status, release version, artifact maturity, and work completion are independent. Changing the overall state remains a separate Owner decision.

p.WORKER-REFINEMENT: An executor receives a bounded packet with exact sources, task, allowed route, read and write scope, resources, checks, and stop boundary. It refines subwork within that route without asking the Owner at every step. New authority, changed final acceptance, or crossing the boundary becomes a concrete coordinator proposal. The coordinator resolves ordinary delegated technical refinements; a worker does not accept its own result.

p.PARALLEL-EXECUTION: Independent ready tasks, bounded parts of one task, preparation, and verification of stable candidates may run in parallel. Actual read and write subjects, shared interfaces, resources, and one integration owner are bound before launch. Different filenames do not prove independence. The work window is limited by capacity to accept and integrate results; heavy commands are coordinated separately from executor count.

p.VERIFICATION-ECONOMY: Select the affected build or test target and required cases first, including negative cases, invariants, and interface consumers. Valid evidence is reused only on the same material input. The full panel is not required per stage, worker, commit, or publication; it remains for an explicitly required final gate or justified cross-cutting impact. Mutation testing is used only for a concrete suspicion, with expected value and an attempt limit recorded.

p.CENTRAL-ACCEPTANCE: The coordinator reads the actual result, compares it with the mandate and architecture, checks sufficient evidence, and only then changes acceptance. Independent review is selected for a material question and expected value rather than every line. A restart or new worker does not erase accepted history. A parent does not close merely because child rows are green when integration or obligations remain unverified.

p.RECOVERY: After failure, quota loss, or account change, ZAP restores the charter, plan, evidence, current stage, debts, and live jobs. An unknown operation outcome is reconciled through receipt, job ID, or postconditions before repeating the effect. Lost reasoning is rebuilt from stored facts; hidden thoughts are not promised durable. Retries and diagnostics belong to the prior logical operation rather than a new session.

p.RETRY-AND-CONTINUATION: The coordinator distinguishes transient overload, no quota, an invalid request, and a product defect. It respects server hints and actual harness retries and does not stack independent infinite loops. Another account does not reset history or authorize moving secrets. Future continuation exists only through an actually configured authorized runtime; the specification does not promise an unstarted timer or background agent.

p.DOCUMENTATION-AND-CHANGE: Changes preserve links among old and new behavior, affected users, migration, documentation, and verification. External documentation is connected only after defining source, revision, write owner, and build rules. A new revision rebinds only affected subjects and evidence. Temporary plans are removed after permanent requirements and unique knowledge move to project sources.

p.CAMPAIGN-CLOSURE: Closure compares original intent, the active authorized outcome revision, and actual benefit. It distinguishes original success, an achieved authorized approximation, partial result, and unattainability under current conditions. It requires truthful dispositions for original and current obligations, acceptance of required results, integration, closure of applicable deferrals, permanent knowledge placement, and a current final gate. An abandoned artifact need not be productized for an obsolete list; its real effects and the inapplicability of old formalities are checked. Empty frontier or exhausted quota is not success, and deleting hard items does not fulfill obligations.

p.METHOD-RESEARCH-PROVENANCE: Research provenance records which external sources informed this work. ZAP requirements were authored independently for this project; external instructions received no authority. This is provenance disclosure, not a claim of formal clean-room certification.
